hero.title: Buy the right GPU system.
hero.description: We align GPU servers and workstations with your product vision, the models you need and your developers’ expertise. Test before you buy, then deploy and improve the system as your business grows.
hero.note: Founder experience in aerospace data-center procurement and government AI procurement.

pains.title: Your hardware choice shapes what your team can deliver.
pains.description: The wrong purchase can force your developers into avoidable engineering work, delay your roadmap and make the product you planned harder to deliver.

items.pain: Will this system support our product vision?
items.impact: Enough GPU memory does not mean your model will run. The model, software and hardware must work together—and fit the way your developers build.
items.solution: We translate your product goals into model, software and hardware requirements, taking your developers’ expertise and existing tools into account.
items.outcome: A system plan that supports your roadmap and reduces avoidable engineering work.

items.pain: How will our workloads perform on these GPUs?
items.impact: A specification sheet cannot show how your application will behave under real demand. Finding the limits after purchase can mean rework or more spending.
items.solution: We can benchmark your workloads on the specific GPUs you are considering before you buy. We test compatibility, response times and how many requests the system can handle, then tune the software.
items.outcome: Measured results to inform the purchase, with limitations identified before you commit.

items.pain: What happens when our AI needs change?
items.impact: Keeping up with weekly model and software changes can pull your team away from improving your product and business workflows.
items.solution: We evaluate relevant new models, optimize how your workloads run and manage agreed infrastructure improvements. Your team can focus on its domain expertise, business workflows and return on investment.
items.outcome: Ongoing technical help that keeps infrastructure work from consuming your product team’s attention.

faq.title: Good questions.

items.question: Do you sell hardware or advise on purchases?
items.answer: We advise on purchases. If you want help with sourcing, we can work with multiple vendors and resellers to coordinate OEM products, delivery and installation. The proposal identifies who supplies the hardware, who installs it and the associated costs.

items.question: Can we start with just a quote review?
items.answer: Yes. The GPU Purchase Review is a separate engagement. You receive a written recommendation and decide whether you want vendor coordination, deployment or ongoing help.

items.question: Can we test performance before buying hardware?
items.answer: Yes. We can benchmark your workloads on the specific GPUs you are considering, testing whether the models and software work together and measuring response times, capacity and running costs. We agree the test configuration and budget upfront, then document the results and anything still to validate on the complete system.

items.question: Is enough GPU memory all we need to run a model?
items.answer: No. Memory is one requirement. The model’s software must also support the GPU and work with the rest of the system. We assess those dependencies alongside your developers’ tools and expertise, then scope tests to check that the proposed setup can deliver your product requirements.

items.question: We already own GPUs. Can you help?
items.answer: Yes. We can assess your hardware, models and inference software, identify compatibility or performance gaps, and scope improvements against the workloads you need to run.

items.question: Can you help after deployment?
items.answer: Yes. We can evaluate new models, optimize workloads, plan upgrades and fallback options, and help your team build operating skills. This gives your developers more time to focus on product features and business workflows. Ongoing work has an agreed scope, schedule and support responsibilities, separate from the purchase review.

items.question: Why involve SonarWave alongside our IT team or vendor?
items.answer: We turn your product vision into software and hardware requirements, then use agreed workload tests to assess the proposed system. Our founder brings aerospace data-center procurement, government AI procurement and production GenAI experience. Your team and vendors gain a practical basis for decisions that goes beyond the specification sheet.

items.question: How are pricing and vendor coordination handled?
items.answer: We agree the service scope, fee and schedule before work starts. Hardware, licences and cloud usage are separate. If vendor coordination is included, the proposal sets out purchasing, installation and support responsibilities and costs.

items.question: Does on-premises AI keep all our data local?
items.answer: That depends on the full setup. External APIs, telemetry, model downloads and access controls need to be reviewed. We plan the deployment around your data requirements; running a model locally does not by itself guarantee privacy or compliance.

sample.title: What a GPU Purchase Review covers.
sample.description: This is an example of the review format, not a client report or a hardware recommendation. Your review is based on your workloads, quotes and agreed scope.
sample.scenario: Example brief: a team wants a local AI assistant for internal documents and is comparing GPU server quotes.

sections.title: 1. Requirements
sections.description: Record the product vision, required features, models, developer expertise and existing software. Connect these to user demand, response-time needs, data restrictions and budget.

sections.title: 2. Quote assessment
sections.description: Assess whether the proposed hardware supports the required models and software, beyond GPU memory alone. Check facilities, networking, storage, warranty and vendor assumptions.

sections.title: 3. Installation readiness
sections.description: Check power, cooling, rack or workstation space, network access and who owns installation and system access.

sections.title: 4. Tests on target GPUs, if scoped
sections.description: Test agreed workloads on the GPUs being considered. Report compatibility findings, response times, request capacity and running costs, with the test conditions and any limits on applying the results to the complete system.

sections.title: 5. Recommendation & validation
sections.description: Explain the recommended direction, unresolved risks and compatibility and performance checks to complete before ordering. Define what the system must demonstrate during acceptance testing.

sample.closing: The outcome is a decision record: how the system supports your product vision, what the evidence shows and what still needs to be checked before you commit.
